name: Home firewall
description: MikroTik's own default firewall: the router answers only the LAN, the internet reaches nothing it did not ask for, and the LAN is masqueraded. MikroDash's address is accepted before the drop.

name: DNS and time
description: Which DNS servers the router asks, whether it answers DNS for the LAN, and the NTP servers it keeps its clock by.

name: Family-safe DNS
description: Resolvers that filter adult and malicious sites, with every DNS query from the LAN redirected to the router so a device set to another resolver is filtered too. Pair it with a firewall template: this makes the router answer DNS.

name: Isolate a network
description: For IoT devices or guests: the network reaches the internet but not the rest of the LAN, and not the router's management services.

name: Anti-bufferbloat (CAKE)
description: Keeps latency low while the line is busy: CAKE on a queue set a little below the line's real speed, so the queue forms in the router rather than the modem.

name: Privacy essentials
description: Switches off UPnP, the web and SOCKS proxies and the bandwidth-test server, and keeps neighbour discovery and MAC access to the LAN.

name: Office firewall
description: The home baseline, plus a RAW drop of source addresses that can never arrive from the internet legitimately. Private ranges and carrier NAT are left out on purpose: many WAN links use them.

name: WireGuard remote access
description: A WireGuard interface for remote staff, its address, and its port opened through the firewall templates' mdcfg-allow hook (deploy the Home or Office firewall first). Add peers on the WireGuard page. Re-applying keeps the interface's key.

name: Fair share per device
description: Every LAN device gets an equal part of the line when it is busy, and all of it when it is not (PCQ).

name: Management lockdown
description: Telnet, FTP and plain web access off; WinBox, SSH and the API reachable only from the admin network, with MikroDash's own address kept in; strong SSH crypto.

name: IPv6 firewall
description: MikroTik's default IPv6 firewall: ICMPv6 and DHCPv6 replies allowed, everything else from outside the LAN dropped.

name: IP stack hardening
description: SYN cookies on, source routing and ICMP redirects refused, loose reverse-path filtering (strict would break multi-WAN).

name: Password policy
description: The length and variety a new or changed router account password must have. Existing passwords are not checked until they change.

variables.name: min_categories
variables.label: Character kinds required (of upper, lower, digit, symbol)

name: Remote syslog
description: Sends the router's info, warning, error and critical log lines to a syslog server as well as keeping them in memory.

name: SNMPv3 read-only
description: A read-only SNMP community with authentication and encryption, readable only from the monitoring server.

name: Site NTP server
description: The router keeps time from an upstream server and serves it to the LAN, so devices without internet access still agree on the time.

name: Add a VLAN network
description: A tagged VLAN on a trunk, with the router's address on it, a DHCP pool and server, and the VLAN in the LAN list so the firewall templates treat it as LAN. Deploy it once per VLAN: each is tagged with its own id, so re-applying one leaves the others alone. Its devices use the router for DNS; pair it with DNS and time.

variables.name: parent_iface
variables.label: Trunk: the interface or bridge the VLAN is tagged on

variables.name: vlan_name
variables.label: Name for the VLAN interface, such as vlan10

variables.name: gateway
variables.label: The router's address on the VLAN

name: Guest network
description: A guest VLAN with its own addresses, DHCP and public DNS, that reaches the internet but not the LAN and not the router. It stays out of the LAN list, and its devices get public resolvers because a firewall template drops DNS to the router from anything that is not LAN.

variables.name: parent_iface
variables.label: Trunk: the interface or bridge the VLAN is tagged on

variables.name: gateway
variables.label: The router's address on the guest network

name: Bridge VLAN (trunk and access ports)
description: One VLAN on a VLAN-filtering bridge: tagged on the trunk ports, untagged on the access ports, each access port moved into the VLAN, then VLAN filtering switched on. Deploy it once per VLAN. Moving ports between VLANs can cut MikroDash off, so every deploy arms the automatic revert.

variables.name: tagged_ports
variables.label: Tagged: the bridge itself (if the router has an address on this VLAN) and each trunk port

name: Home, IoT and Guest VLANs
description: A whole home network on one bridge: Home, IoT and Guest VLANs, each with its own addresses and DHCP, behind a complete firewall that REPLACES the router's filter rules. Home reaches the internet, the router and IoT; IoT reaches the internet and Home only on the ports you choose; Guest reaches the internet only. Rules for anything else, such as VPN ports, are removed: add them back afterwards. Manage the router from Home afterwards. Wi-Fi joins a VLAN through its own VLAN setting.

variables.name: tagged_ports
variables.label: Tagged on all three VLANs: the bridge itself and any trunk ports

variables.label: First address DHCP hands out on Home

variables.name: home_pool_end
variables.label: Last address DHCP hands out on Home

variables.name: iot_pool_start
variables.label: First address DHCP hands out on IoT

variables.name: iot_pool_end
variables.label: Last address DHCP hands out on IoT

variables.name: guest_pool_start
variables.label: First address DHCP hands out on Guest

variables.name: guest_pool_end
variables.label: Last address DHCP hands out on Guest

variables.label: TCP ports IoT devices may open on Home (Home Assistant, MQTT)
